messages.text:
The proposal raises Team from $99 to $129 and Business from $249 to $299. Existing customers need separate treatment: two November renewals are already too close for 30 days’ notice, one account has a fixed-rate commitment, and one keeps a recurring 20% discount.

I’m building a customer-by-customer preview, revenue scenarios, and notice drafts. The materials are a synthetic snapshot, so the result will be a prepared rollout package; live billing still needs verification.

Understood. I’ll prepare a simulation and handoff package with the notice date left unresolved. I’ll show clearly labeled timing examples and make the model rerunnable once a date is chosen; none of those dates will be treated as approved or sent.

The modeled active-customer baseline is $484.70/month. If all four active accounts eventually renew at the proposed rates, it becomes $610.37/month—a $125.67 increase. That excludes the past-due account and pending cancellation, and assumes the CSV amounts are before discounts.

The Ultrametric progress save was blocked because the tool requires approval and this session’s approval policy is set to “never.” I’ll keep the work in local files.

The timing examples now preserve each commitment. With hypothetical notice on October 12, Elm and Canal move in December, Maple in February, and Willow at its March annual renewal. With notice on November 15, Elm and Canal move to January.

The downside is also material: losing Elm at its increase would erase the eventual revenue gain across the four active accounts. I’m including that sensitivity alongside the retained-customer forecast.
